spec.requirement: A test obligation's `path` and `selector` are repository-relative and resolve inside the repository that CONSUMES the corpus: a consumer repository's own git-tracked test file is accepted by `spec validate` and `spec check`, and `spec bundle` returns that `path` and `selector` verbatim with the registered runner's argv vector. `--repo-root DIR` names the consuming repository when the corpus lives outside it. With no resolvable root the run refuses (`unresolvable-repo-root`) rather than grading the obligation against Auger's own checkout.
spec.verification: Builds a fresh consumer repository with its own tracked `tests/test_marker.py`, validates and checks the corpus that names it, and asserts the bundle carries `path="tests/test_marker.py"` and `selector="test_marker"` with no Auger path in the resolved fields. Rolling this behaviour back is exercised by the same tracked test (`rollback="tracked-test"`, AUG-143).

Points a corpus outside any work tree at `tests/test_xml_specs.py`, which exists and is tracked in Auger's own checkout, and asserts the run refuses with `unresolvable-repo-root` and names `--repo-root` as the fix.
spec.requirement: A `<verification>` or `<test>` block that points at a test carries `runner`, `path` and `selector` together. `runner` is an identifier in Auger's registry — today only `pytest` — serialized to the argv vector `<current Python> -m pytest`; anything else, including a shell string such as `bash -c`, is refused (`invalid-test-ref`), so XML never executes a command.
spec.verification: Asserts a resolved obligation's runner is the argv list `[sys.executable, "-m", "pytest"]`, then writes a `<test runner="bash -c">` obligation and asserts validation refuses it with `invalid-test-ref`. Nothing is written to a repository on this path, so there is no rollback to exercise — declared, not left to a reader's guess (`rollback="unsupported"`, AUG-143).
